paragraphs: Week 3 (Sept 18 – 22, Lectures 5 and 6) Teaching and Learning

3.2 The derivative as a function: differentiability at a point and on a domain (convention: f is differentiable on its domain if it is differentiable at every interior point and is one-sided differentiable at every endpoint in the domain); differentiability implies continuity.
3.3 Differentiation rules: derivatives of constant functions; linearity (sum rule + constant multiple rule); power rule; product rule; quotient rule; second- and higher-order derivatives.
3.4 The derivative as a rate of change: motion along a line (displacement, velocity, speed, acceleration, and jerk); derivatives in economics.
3.5 Derivatives of trigonometric functions: the derivatives of sin, cos, tan, cot, sec, and csc.
3.6 Chain rule: the chain rule (its formal proof can be postponed until 3.9 is covered).
